claims.text: The initial catalyst is a near-equiatomic multi-principal-element automotive alloy catalyst.
The unmodified catalyst has good intrinsic catalytic activity.
The unmodified catalyst is susceptible to poisoning by species such as H2O and NO.
The unmodified catalyst has durability problems during transient, low-temperature operation.
A thin, nanometer-scale CeO2 overlayer will enable low-temperature oxidation activity.
A thin CeO2 overlayer will increase resistance to exhaust-gas poisoning.
A thin CeO2 overlayer will improve the catalyst's long-term durability.
CeO2 provides oxygen-storage capacity through oxygen vacancies and mobile oxygen species.
The CeO2 overlayer physically protects the alloy catalyst against sintering.
The CeO2 overlayer physically protects the alloy catalyst against structural degradation.
The CeO2 overlayer supplies mobile oxygen at low temperatures, thereby enhancing oxidation reactions.
The CeO2 overlayer scavenges poisoning species, thereby enhancing oxidation reactions.
The CeO2 overlayer acts as a stable barrier that mitigates structural degradation during thermal cycling.
Adding the CeO2 overlayer does not require an increase in platinum-group-metal content.
The CeO2-modified catalyst will have a lower CO and hydrocarbon light-off temperature than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-modified catalyst will maintain higher CO and hydrocarbon conversion in the presence of H2O and NO than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-modified catalyst will preserve its structure better during accelerated aging than the unmodified catalyst.
The CeO2-modified catalyst will retain its catalytic activity better during accelerated aging than the unmodified catalyst.
The predicted benefits apply under conventional automotive exhaust compositions at temperatures below 150 °C.
The predicted benefits persist over aging conditions approximating a vehicle's lifetime mileage.
